success.description: Full AES256 master-key recovery within named model M8. Section5.2 enumerates all128 bits of K8 and reuses the seven-round matching construction. Adopt the intended corrected factorization, correct coordinates and recorded boundary interpretation, with any complete equivalent K7 converted back by its known invertible linear boundary transform. For the true K8 branch, each of four targets uses all already acquired n2 structures and has Equation7 miss bound \((1-n_1^{-1})^{n_2}\). The stronger extension premise requires a uniform raw wrong-signature law conditional on the setup for every fixed wrong outer/inner tuple, including wrong K8 guesses. This is an explicit heuristic model premise, not implied by conditioning the seven-round model on correct K8 and not proved for actual AES. The raw256-byte signature has2048 bits. With at most \(2^{200}/n_1\) table entries, a modeled wrong hit has probability at most \(2^{-1848}/n_1\). A fixed superset of at most \(4n_2 2^{208}\) outer/inner tests includes the128-bit outer K8 enumeration and80-bit target search. The aggregate wrong-hit term is consequently \(2^{-1638}n_2/n_1\), not the seven-round exponent1766. Union bounding four true-target misses and all wrong hits gives \(p_{\mathcal M_8,\mathrm{key}}\ge\max\{0,1-4(1-n_1^{-1})^{n_2}-2^{-1638}n_2/n_1\}\), without cross-target or cross-guess independence. Within-target sampling assumptions remain. Once all groups identify correct K7 and the enumerated K8, their eight consecutive words w28..w35 recover the master key: FIPS Algorithm2 has \(w_i=w_{i-8}\oplus T_i(w_{i-1})\); applying the same XOR equation backward for i35 down to8 uniquely recovers w0..w7. This exact inversion needs no residual key enumeration. It is not an inference that168/200 selected-material bits are independent master-key bits. The complete-table assignment n1=n2=1 retains the positive failure term symbolically, not rounded to100%. Applicability still requires nonempty finite tables, positive integer usable n2, feasible query allocation and the source matching-work estimate. Original source conflicts, native units and domain limits remain. verified concerns the mathematical implication inside M8 and the output/budget mapping, not an experiment, an unconditional AES bound, a fixed-time guarantee or complete parameter-domain feasibility.

evidence.interpretation: AES256 uses Nk=8 and w_i=w_(i-8) XOR T_i(w_(i-1)). Given consecutive w28..w35 (ordinary K7/K8), evaluating i35 down to8 recovers w0..w7 uniquely. If the matching boundary returns an equivalent full K7, apply its public invertible linear conversion first. This universal algebraic recurrence, not the earlier finite64-key check alone, establishes deterministic completion after correct identification. It supplies no probability of obtaining those correct round keys.
